text: The Dread King

The Dread King was a Dark Lord of Nagash – one of the most powerful followers of the Great Necromancer. Little is known about his past before serving Nagash. Originating somewhere in the southern Old World, he conquered the fertile lands around the Mortis Delta in the name of his master and was rewarded with an aura of dread and an undead dragon. Eventually, he was slain and buried in a pyramid in Nehekhara. Centuries later, he returned to this world, causing the dead to rise from their graves across the Old World.
The Hand of Nagash

His name long lost to time, the being known as the Hand of Nagash was once a mortal necromancer, who rose to become one of the Dark Lords – the most trusted servants of the Great Necromancer, Nagash. Such was the devastation and ruin he caused in his master's name that his victims came to dread him as the 'Hand of Nagash', and he has borne no other name since. Long thought defeated and entombed within the ice of Troll Country, the Dread King's hosts recently found and resurrected him. Once more, he rides his chariot across the Old World to spread destruction and terror in Nagash's name.
Gunther Larenscheld

Gunther Larenscheld was once a wizard of the Celestial College in Altdorf. He discovered the Grimoire Necris – an ancient tome written by the necromancer Van Damneg – and became obsessed with its power. His secret experiments strengthened his sorcery until he succeeded in reincarnating the life force within a human corpse. Larenscheld's obsession drove him to break into the sealed vaults of the Temple of Sigmar in Altdorf, attempting to steal the Books of Nagash and the Liber Mortis. He now searches for the resting place of the Dread King in his quest for eternal life and unlimited power, believing the Dark Lord of Nagash will grant him perfect unlife should he pledge himself to his service.

Undead soldiers who make up the majority of the Legion of Terror. These warriors fight in a manner reminiscent of an ancient civilisation from the Black Peninsula. Equipped with large round shields and spears and clad in bronze armour, they form tight formations that are difficult to overcome, marching forward unflinchingly and thrusting their spears tirelessly into their foes.

Exotic creatures hailing from the lush bushlands between Araby and the jungles of the Southlands. The ferocious and dangerous animals have a peculiar habit of instinctively travelling to specific places to die when they reach a certain age. These elephant graveyards are a treasure trove for any necromancer, who can find countless corpses there for reanimation. The henchmen of the Dread King control many such places, ensuring a steady supply of war beasts.
Legion of Terror

The undead hosts of the Dread King, Dark Lord of Nagash, the Legion of Terror is an oddity amongst the Great Necromancer's servants. Undead soldiers from a long-lost civilisation in the southern Old World, the archaic style of their armour and fighting formations evokes the warriors depicted in the ruins of Luccini and Myrmidens. Their armies specialise in heavy phalanxes of pikes, supported by skirmishers and powerful shock cavalry.

The origin of the Dread King and his undead hosts is quite unclear. Scholars who have studied the archaic armaments they wield in battle suggest a similarity to the styles of warriors depicted in frescoes found in ancient ruins dotting the southern Old World, especially in the cities of Luccini and Myrmidens.

The Dread King was once a mortal ruler hailing from the southern Old World, somewhere between the Black Peninsula and Tilea. He set out to conquer the desert lands of Nehekhara at the head of a great host of disciplined warriors, and it was there that he encountered Nagash. The Great Necromancer made him an offer: swear loyalty, and he would become the greatest conqueror the world had ever seen. The King accepted and was infused with the power of unlife, an aura of absolute dread, and a mighty zombie dragon as his personal mount. For countless years, he conquered in his master's name until he was finally struck down. Now, he has risen again, and nothing will stop the Dread King and his Army of Darkness.
